text:
Maya (PM): FYI — Acme (enterprise, dedicated) just opened a P1: after yesterday's runtime kernel tweak we pushed, a subset of requests to their dedicated pool are getting 504s or truncated streams. They see ~1% of requests failing but it hits their latency-sensitive flow. Asking for ETA and whether this needs a hotfix.
Jordan (Support): They attached logs — repeatable on dev with a longer prefix and streaming=on. I sent the snippet to Alex.
Alex (Eng): Looking. Initial guess: kernel change to KV cache eviction path + streaming path race. Could cause the runtime to drop the response and return 504 instead of retry.
Priya (Eng-SRE): Severity assessment: customer impact is high for them but limited to specific sequences. Risk of regression if we revert broadly.
Sam (Sales): Acme is asking for an expedited fix; they threatened to pause traffic if not resolved in 48h. We should weigh reputation risk.
Ellie (Customer Success): They're on a dedicated contract with SLA credits. CS wants transparent comms and a temporary workaround.
Maya (PM): Options: 1) Hotfix revert the kernel tweak to all Dedicated pools (fast, higher blast radius). 2) Targeted canary rollback for Acme's pool and a few at-risk customers (slower but safer). 3) Ship an app-level mitigation toggle and schedule next normal release. Thoughts?
Alex (Eng): Reverting across all pools is ~2-3hr work + full verification but quick. Targeted rollback to Acme's pool is ~30-60m and low risk if we have good routing flags. We already have per-customer pool flags.
Priya (Eng-SRE): How confident are we that the kernel tweak is the root cause? We saw similar but not identical stacktraces. I'll run a deeper diff and enable extra tracing in canary.
Jordan (Support): Workaround for Acme: disable streaming on their requests -> avoids the streaming codepath causing the race. They said streaming is critical, but temporary acceptable.
Sam (Sales): If a temporary workaround is an option, we can buy time for a safer canary. Acme prefers a rollback only on their pool if possible.
Maya (PM): Decision proposal: do a targeted rollback on Acme's dedicated pool (hotfix scoped to customer) + enable tracing dashboard, notify customer with timeline. If rollback isn't possible within 2h, instruct them to disable streaming as a temporary mitigation.
Alex (Eng): I can own the targeted rollback. Steps: 1) snapshot current config, 2) pin older runtime kernel on their pool, 3) run smoke tests, 4) flip routing, 5) monitor. Rollback window estimate 45m.
Priya (Eng-SRE): I'll prepare canary monitors and open an adhoc incident channel for 15m and 1h checks. Add SLO metrics diff and error-rate alerts.
Maya (PM): Comms plan: notify Acme (Ellie) with expected 45–60m rollback start, explain why, and offer the streaming toggle if they prefer immediate mitigation. Internal comm: inform @eng-oncall and @support.
Ellie (Customer Success): I'll draft the customer message. Keep it clear: targeted rollback, no config changes required on their side, risk minimal.
Sam (Sales): I want to be on the customer call after rollback completes. Will join.
Alex (Eng): Preparing rollback now. Patch to pin kernel SHA -> config snippet: 
```
runtime.kernel.version: 2026-03-18-aa7f
routing.policy.pool: "acme-dedicated-eu"
```
I'll push and run smoke.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout job started for pool acme-dedicated-eu -> job id 93422.
Priya (Eng-SRE): Smoke results: token roundtrips fine on 10k synthetic requests, error rate 0.03% (baseline). Observability dashboards look stable.
Alex (Eng): Flipping routing to pinned kernel now.
deploy-bot: Routing flip completed for pool acme-dedicated-eu. Canary status: healthy.
Jordan (Support): Acme confirms lower errors on their end. They see streaming restored.
Maya (PM): Great. Postmortem next steps: schedule regression test for streaming+kv cache permutations, add a regression guard into release checklist, and consider a toggle to disable the new eviction heuristics per pool.
Priya (Eng-SRE): I'll file the incident and assign action items for postmortem. Low effort mitigation: expose runtime flag to disable new eviction. Medium-term: tighter test harness.
Alex (Eng): I'll prepare a follow-up PR to add the per-pool eviction toggle and add unit+integration tests for streaming edge cases.
Ellie (Customer Success): Sharing final note to Acme: rollback completed, monitoring in place, will follow up with root cause postmortem within 72h.
Maya (PM): Thanks everyone. Closing this thread once PRs and postmortem are scheduled. :thumbsup:
